geometry_edits.rationale: Retype the dominant mass into a split-wing macro to create a true void and stronger hierarchical section for neighborhood living.
Split along the long axis so the open figure can align with the street/access side.
Enlarge the separation to make the court/void materially legible.
Maintain one continuous building with a controlled connector, preventing the form from reading as detached fragments.
Introduce a ground spine so the threshold becomes public and programmatic at the access edge.

graph_edits.rationale: Retype the dominant mass away from a blunt cantilever toward a split-wing/courtyard structure so the street edge can open and the section can support neighborhood-living public threshold logic.
Use the long axis to separate the mass into readable wings, creating room for a meaningful void/court aligned to the access edge.
Increase separation enough to make the void legible as usable public space rather than a shallow notch.
Keep the composition as one building by reconnecting the split with a controlled bridge condition instead of detached fragments.
Add a ground-level spine so the access edge reads as a public threshold and not a sealed wall.
Give the ground connection enough width to function as active frontage/entry rather than a token seam.

rationale: The candidate is a compact, coherent mass in each single view, but the four-view set does not resolve into a convincing neighborhood-living figure. The object reads more like a blunt cantilevered block with shallow stepbacks than a building whose ground edge actively engages the verified frontage. The parcel is contained, but the access side remains visually sealed or weakly articulated, and the courtyard/terrace language is too small to count as a meaningful public void. The silhouette is acceptable as an early massing, but it lacks the section depth and public-threshold consequence expected by the program. In particular, the geometry feels closer to a generic stacked/offset object than to a compact mixed-use street building with a legible entry sequence and usable open ground.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Tower-like composition and vertical emphasis are not well aligned with neighborhood_living ground-threshold needs.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Tapered/stepped overall mass can still read as a single dominant gesture when the profile is coherent across views.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office-tower typology and slender high-rise section are not transferable to this compact street-building brief.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single strong vertical profile can organize a mass and produce legibility in elevation.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Low single-story restaurant mass is too small and too pavilion-like for the requested 5-floor neighborhood building.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A clear public-facing ground edge with a canopy/void-like threshold strengthens program legibility.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is much more sectional and expansive than the candidate; use its void/terrace principle, not its large footprint.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Continuous inhabited terrace and courtyard logic can support neighborhood living when the void and section are integral to the mass.

warnings: Primary access edge is not clearly answered by a public void, court, notch, or undercut.
The form is read more as a closed extrusion with a minor fracture than as a sectionally programmed neighborhood building.
There is no strong evidence of a usable public ground-space figure.
Potential typological drift toward an abstract block/cantilever rather than active neighborhood living massing.
